answer_1.quote: We extend standard LLM-as-a-Judge baselines ... across a range of response domains that are typically challenging for LLM-as-a-Judge systems: (1) long-form factual, (2) advanced coding, and (3) math responses.
answer_1.outputs: pairwise preference judgments (which response is better)

answer_3.quote: Pairwise feedback is widely used to understand LLM performance on complex tasks... given a prompt and two possible responses, the annotator decides which response is "better".

answer_4.quote: We also collect human preference annotations from 3 annotators over the entire new dataset, and these annotators, on average, agree with 76.83% of those ground-truth annotations when not selecting a tie.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to select which of the two responses is preferred (or indicate a tie).
